summary: Add GET /api/alerts/trends with bounded days query validation and oldest-first UTC daily severity buckets for dashboard trend charts.
constraints: Keep the change in the existing controller -> service -> repository -> EF Core slice.
Use a query DTO with existing data-annotation validation patterns so invalid days values produce 400 ValidationProblemDetails consistently.
days defaults to 7 and must accept only 1 through 90 inclusive.
Return one bucket per UTC calendar day for the last N days in oldest-first order.
Every bucket must include zero-count days and zero-count severities.
Severity ordering must stay aligned with the summary endpoint convention: Low, Medium, High, Critical.
No schema or migration work is expected for this story.
coverage_goals: Controller coverage for the new trends action, days defaulting expectations, and bad-request behavior for invalid query values.
Service coverage for oldest-first bucket ordering, zero-filled missing UTC days, and zero-filled severity counts in summary-consistent order.
Repository coverage for UTC date-window filtering and per-day per-severity aggregation.
implementation_assumptions: Last N days includes the current UTC calendar day plus the previous N - 1 UTC days.
Alert CreatedDate values already follow the repository's existing UTC convention and should be grouped by UTC calendar date.
The service layer should handle zero-filling of missing dates and severities unless implementation discovers a cleaner existing pattern.
If controller-unit coverage cannot prove non-numeric query binding behavior, implementation may add one focused WebApplicationFactory API test and then update this cache.
